data.description:
## Observation

On 2026-11-17, I ran `python -m rebar verify-identity --all` in enforced mode (`REBAR_IDENTITY_REQUIRE_AUTHENTICATED=1`) on a TMPDIR dry-run copy of the reclaimed tickets history. The copy came from `origin/tickets` e7a0476397f, collapsed with a 30-day horizon. The python process sat at 0% CPU, polling a pipe, while a child ran:

`git log --diff-filter=A --full-history --no-renames --format=%H -- *<position>*`

That child was at about 98% CPU, one ledger position at a time.

This is the per-position fallback `authorship.resolve_position_commit`, called from `_resolve_position` in `src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py` when `build_position_commit_map` has no entry. After a reclaim, no commit on the rewritten branch adds a below-checkpoint event's file. Every such ledger position therefore misses the batched map and costs one full-history walk. An earlier run of the same command on the same copy had not finished after about 3.5 hours.

## What is not established

- The miss count, and the share of the runtime it accounts for, have not been measured.
- The advisory mode that CI uses today (`require_authenticated = false`) is O(events). It finished in seconds on the same copy, reporting 49,438 signed and 874 unsigned events (50,312 in scope), identical before and after the reclaim.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Root cause measured on a dry-run copy: the number of fallback calls, and the runtime with and without them.
- [ ] Enforced `verify-identity --all` on a reclaimed copy of the real store completes in time comparable to the same run on the unreclaimed copy, shown by timing both on one dry-run workdir.
data.title: verify-identity on a reclaimed store runs a full-history git log per below-checkpoint ledger entry
